pairs.subject: public-claim-provenance
pairs.evidence: app/jds/[slug]/page.tsx:255 The public share page prints 'Saved {date}' from jds.created_at, which updateJd/revertJd never update (app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:415 only sets title/body), so after any edit the candidate-facing date is a stand-in that answers 'when created', not 'when saved', although the honest source jdLastEditedAt exists and this page already loads it for translation freshness (page.tsx:35).

techniques.evidence: app/jds/[slug]/page.tsx:255 The only value that looks derived on this public page is a date taken from a proxy (the creation timestamp) under a 'Saved' label. The technique's proxy rule says a value derived from a proxy is worse than a typed one, because it looks derived while answering a different question. The real target (jdLastEditedAt, MAX(jd_revisions.created_at)) is derivable, so the fix is to read it rather than to label the date.

messages/en.json:10037 Rendered to candidates whenever Apply is closed (jdPublicHeader.ts:12 pushes notAccepting regardless of canManage), including archived JDs (isPublicJdApplyOpen is false on archivedAt). There 'yet' implies an opening no mechanism will deliver, beside the archived banner. Conformant parts: Apply is gated on isJobOpenForApplications (page.tsx:201), and the alternates offer only served languages.
app/jds/[slug]/page.tsx:186 The only public count (the candidates header count) was removed for privacy. No fraction or count renders on the page, so there is no numerator/denominator to sort.

app/jds/[slug]/page.tsx:147 A per-request server component renders one row's content. No count is reduced from a heavy catalog, and no catalog crosses into the client bundle (JdBody receives only the markdown string).
app/jds/[slug]/page.tsx:176 There is no live counter or liveness badge. The read-failure path shows an explicit error rather than a seeded value, so a failure looks like a failure.

app/jds/[slug]/JdBody.tsx:23 There is no derived count against an authored target and no ratio. The lockstep rule is honoured anyway: one boolean drives both the copy button and the empty-state placeholder.

pairs.registryProposal: The proxy rule sits in no-data-source-labelled-inline, whose precondition is a value that 'cannot be derived and must be typed', and the 'derive from the target, never from a stand-in' rule sits in build-time-derivation, whose precondition is a heavy catalog. A public timestamp or field derived from the wrong column of an otherwise light source (a creation date under a 'Saved'/'Updated' label) matches neither precondition cleanly. The 'never from a stand-in' rule could be lifted into the golden path, or into derived-numerator's procedure, so it binds every derived public value.
